questions.question: What was India's rank in the 2025 Human Development Index (HDI) released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**130**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India ranked **130th** in the 2025 Human Development Index (HDI) released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The HDI measures a country's overall achievement in three key dimensions of human development: **health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling),** and **standard of living (Gross National Income per capita).**
 
• India's ranking reflects its progress in areas such as health and education, but it also highlights the need for improvements in income equality and access to quality services.
 
• The HDI report for 2025 focused on the post-pandemic recovery and its impact on global and national development indicators, emphasizing the need for sustainable and inclusive growth.
 
• Countries with a higher HDI ranking demonstrate better human development outcomes, with India categorized under the "medium human development" group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• The HDI is a composite index introduced by the UNDP in 1990 to measure and compare levels of development across countries.
 
• It considers three dimensions: **health (life expectancy at birth), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling),** and **standard of living (measured by Gross National Income per capita adjusted for purchasing power parity).**
 
• The HDI provides a comprehensive picture of a country's development, beyond just economic growth.

questions.question: Which of the following initiatives were launched by the Department of Posts in May 2025 to modernise India’s addressing system and enhance last-mile delivery?

options.text: India Address Precision System and Postal Service Enhancer
GeoLocate India and Postal Code Finder
Know Your DIGIPIN and Know Your PIN Code web platforms
Digital India Address Mapping and National Postal Tracker

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Know Your DIGIPIN and Know Your PIN Code web platforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Department of Posts launched the **Know Your DIGIPIN and Know Your PIN Code web platforms** in May 2025 to modernize India's addressing system.
 
• These platforms aim to enhance last-mile delivery by introducing a digital and precise addressing mechanism for postal services.
 
• **Know Your DIGIPIN** is designed to complement India's existing PIN code system by assigning unique digital identifiers to addresses, ensuring better accuracy in location mapping.
 
• **Know Your PIN Code** integrates advanced geospatial technology, allowing users to locate their postal codes and understand address-specific delivery zones.
 
• The initiative aligns with the broader goals of the **Digital India program** by leveraging technology for efficient postal and delivery services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PIN code (Postal Index Number)**

 
 
• A PIN code (Postal Index Number) is the traditional 6-digit numeric code introduced in 1972 to sort mail into broad geographical zones.
 
• It helps route mail to the correct post office but lacks specific, doorstep-level accuracy, as one PIN code can cover an entire neighborhood or multiple villages. 
 
 
 
• **DIGIPIN (Digital Postal Index Number)**
 
 
• A DIGIPIN (Digital Postal Index Number), launched in May 2025, is a modern 10-character alphanumeric code that provides precise, GPS-level location accuracy, down to an approximate 4x4 meter area.
 
• Developed by India Post in collaboration with IIT Hyderabad and ISRO, it is a geospatial identifier that complements the existing PIN code system.
 
• The DIGIPIN is an open-source system designed to improve last-mile delivery, enhance emergency responses, and support digital services across India.
 
• Users can find their DIGIPIN through the official India Post portal by using their precise geolocation.

questions.question: Which of the following techniques was used by the Harappans to create bronze sculptures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lost-wax casting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The lost-wax casting technique, also known as **cire perdue**, was widely used by the Harappans for creating intricate bronze sculptures.
 
• In this process, artisans first created a model of the sculpture using wax, which was then encased in clay or another refractory material.
 
• The wax was melted out, leaving a hollow mold that was filled with molten metal, such as bronze, to form the final sculpture.
 
• This method allowed the Harappans to produce highly detailed and sophisticated sculptures, as seen in artifacts like the famous **"Dancing Girl"** of Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• The lost-wax casting technique highlights the advanced metallurgical skills and artistic craftsmanship of the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Engraving:**

 
 
• Engraving is the art of carving designs onto a surface, typically metal, wood, or stone.
 
• This method is more suitable for creating decorative patterns or inscriptions rather than free-standing sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Stone carving:**
 
 
• Stone carving involves shaping stone into desired forms using tools like chisels and hammers.
 
• Although the Harappans were skilled in stone carving, evidenced by seals and architectural remains, this technique was distinct from their methods of creating bronze sculptures.
 
• Stone carving is more commonly associated with sculptures and monuments in other cultures, such as Egyptian and Greek civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Hand-molding:**
 
 
• Hand-molding refers to directly shaping materials like clay or wax with hands or simple tools.
 
• It is a versatile technique but lacks the precision and complexity achieved through lost-wax casting.
 
• While hand-molding might have been used for preliminary designs.

questions.question: Which of the following changes would need the approval of at least half of all State Legislatures?

options.text: Amending the Emergency provisions in Part XVIII
Changing the Guarantee of Fundamental Rights
Altering the Union List of subjects

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amending the Emergency provisions in Part XVIII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amending the Emergency provisions in Part XVIII of the Indian Constitution requires the approval of at least half of all State Legislatures in addition to parliamentary approval.
 
• This amendment falls under the special category of constitutional amendments as prescribed in Article 368(2) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Provisions such as altering the distribution of powers between the Union and States, including emergency provisions, necessitate consultation and approval from State Legislatures to maintain the federal structure of governance.
 
• Emergency provisions (Articles 352, 356, and 360) have a profound impact on the autonomy of states, making state approval essential for such amendments.
 
• Such requirements highlight the cooperative federalism embedded in India's constitutional framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The key types of majorities:**

 
 
• **Simple Majority** (Functional Majority)

 
 
• Definition: More than 50% of members present and voting.
 
• Use: Most common; for ordinary bills, confidence/no-confidence motions, declaring emergencies. 
 
• Absolute Majority
 
• Definition: More than 50% of the total strength (total members) of the House.
 
• Use: Government formation, certain procedural matters. 
 
 
 
• **Effective Majority**
 
 
• Definition: More than 50% of the effective strength (total strength minus vacancies).
 
• Use: Removing the Speaker/Deputy Speaker, or Vice-President. 
 
 
 
• **Special Majority**
 
 
• Definition: Stronger majorities, varying by Article, often requiring 2/3rds present and voting plus >50% total membership.
 
• Use:
 
 
• Article 368 (Constitutional Amendments): Most significant changes need 2/3rds present & voting + >50% total strength.
 
• Article 368 + State Ratification: For federal provisions, needs Special Majority plus approval from half the state legislatures.
 
• Article 249/368: Other specific constitutional changes.

questions.question: Equal pay for equal work is ensured under which Article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39(d)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 39(d)** of the Indian Constitution directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women as a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It emphasizes eliminating gender discrimination in wages and ensuring equitable treatment in employment opportunities.
 
• This article plays a pivotal role in promoting social justice and economic equality in India.
 
• While DPSPs are not enforceable in a court of law, they provide a framework for governance and guide the State in making laws and policies.
 
• The principle of “equal pay for equal work” has been upheld multiple times by the Supreme Court of India as a fundamental right under the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 43**:

 
 
• Article 43 directs the State to secure a living wage, decent standard of life, and social and cultural opportunities for all workers.
 
• It emphasizes improving the conditions of workers, especially in the unorganized sector, to achieve economic democracy.
 
• It also promotes cottage industries in rural areas to ensure sustainable livelihoods for workers.
 
 
 
• **Article 42**:
 
 
• Article 42 directs the State to make provisions for securing just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
 
• This article ensures dignity and well-being of workers by addressing issues like safe workplaces and maternity benefits for working women.
 
• Laws such as the Maternity Benefit Act and the Factories Act are inspired by this provision.
 
 
 
• **Article 39(a)**:
 
 
• Article 39(a) directs the State to ensure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity.
 
• It mandates the provision of free legal aid to economically weaker sections to ensure access to justice.
 
• It forms the foundation of initiatives like the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

questions.question: Who is described as the 'permanent executive'?

options.text: The permanent civil servants who manage daily administration
The heads of government and their ministers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The permanent civil servants who manage daily administration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'permanent executive' refers to the permanent civil servants who work in various government departments and agencies, ensuring the smooth functioning of day-to-day administration.
 
• Civil servants are professionally trained individuals recruited through competitive examinations, such as the Civil Services Examination conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in India.
 
• They are responsible for implementing government policies, advising ministers, and managing public services across sectors like health, education, defense, and infrastructure.
 
• Their role is apolitical, meaning they are expected to perform their duties without political bias, ensuring continuity and stability in governance regardless of changes in the ruling party.
 
• Their expertise and institutional memory make them essential for the functioning of the government over time, as they remain in office while elected representatives may change periodically.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Members of the elected Parliament**

 
 
• The elected Parliament consists of representatives chosen by the people through democratic elections, such as Members of Parliament (MPs) in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha in India.
 
• They form the legislative branch of the government and are responsible for enacting laws, debating policies, and holding the executive accountable.
 
• Unlike the permanent executive, their tenure is limited to the term of the Parliament (usually five years), after which elections are held again.
 
 
 
• **Judges of the Supreme Court**
 
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are part of the judiciary, which is the third branch of government responsible for interpreting laws, protecting constitutional rights, and resolving disputes.
 
• They are independent of the executive and legislative branches and serve until the age of retirement (65 years in India).
 
• Their primary role is to uphold the rule of law and ensure justice is delivered impartially.
 
 
 
• **The heads of government and their ministers**
 
 
• The heads of government (e.g., Prime Minister, Chief Ministers) and their ministers form the political executive, which is responsible for formulating policies and decisions for governance.
 
• They are elected representatives who hold office for the duration of their government’s term and are accountable to the legislature and the public.
 
• Unlike the permanent executive, their tenure is tied to political outcomes, such as elections or parliamentary confidence.

questions.question: Which of the following quantities has both magnitude and direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Velocity** is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude (speed) and direction.
 
• The formula for velocity is **v = s/t**, where "v" is velocity, "s" is displacement, and "t" is time.
 
• Unlike speed, which is scalar, velocity provides information about the direction of motion along with the rate of displacement.
 
• For instance, if an object moves 10 meters east in 2 seconds, its velocity would be 5 m/s east.
 
• Velocity can be positive, negative, or zero, depending on the direction of motion relative to a chosen reference point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Time**

 
 
• Time is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• It is a fundamental physical quantity that measures the progression of events from the past to the present and into the future.
 
• The SI unit of time is the second (s).
 
• In physics, time plays a crucial role in equations of motion, such as speed = distance/time.
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• Distance is a scalar quantity that measures the total path covered by an object irrespective of direction.
 
• It is always positive and does not decrease, even if the object changes direction.
 
• The SI unit of distance is the meter (m).
 
• For example, if a person walks 5 meters forward and then 3 meters backward, the total distance covered is 8 meters.
 
 
 
• **Speed**
 
 
• Speed is a scalar quantity that represents how fast an object is moving.
 
• The formula for speed is **speed = distance/time**.
 
• Unlike velocity, speed does not include direction; it only indicates the rate of motion.
 
• The SI unit of speed is meters per second (m/s).
 
• For example, a car traveling 60 km in 1 hour has a speed of 60 km/h.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of chemical weathering?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxidation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Oxidation** is a process where oxygen reacts with minerals, particularly metallic elements such as iron, leading to chemical changes in rocks and soil.
 
• This reaction often leads to the formation of oxides, such as rust in iron-bearing minerals, weakening the rock structure and contributing to its breakdown.
 
• Oxidation is a prominent form of chemical weathering observed in environments with sufficient moisture and oxygen availability.
 
• Common examples of oxidation in nature include the reddish coloration seen in rocks containing iron minerals due to the formation of iron oxides.
 
• This process plays a vital role in shaping landscapes and altering the composition of rocks over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frost Action:**

 
 
• Frost action is a physical weathering process where water enters cracks in rocks, freezes, and expands.
 
• The expansion of ice exerts pressure on the rock, causing it to break apart over time.
 
• This process is common in colder climates and contributes to the mechanical breakdown of rocks rather than chemical alteration.
 
 
 
• **Exfoliation:**
 
 
• Exfoliation is a physical weathering process where rocks peel or flake off in sheets due to temperature changes, pressure release, or mechanical stress.
 
• This phenomenon typically occurs in regions with significant diurnal temperature variations, causing rocks to expand during the day and contract at night.
 
 
 
• **Abrasion:**
 
 
• Abrasion is another form of physical weathering where rocks and sediments grind against each other, wearing down surfaces over time.
 
• This process is commonly observed in riverbeds, beaches, or areas with strong winds carrying sand and particles.
 
• Like frost action and exfoliation, abrasion is a mechanical process and does not involve chemical changes in the rock composition.

questions.question: Which key urban feature of Indus Valley cities shows advanced planning with streets intersecting at right angles and covered drains?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Grid-pattern layout** is a hallmark of Indus Valley Civilization cities, showcasing advanced urban planning.
 
• The streets were designed to intersect at right angles, forming a grid system, which ensured organized city planning and efficient movement.
 
• Covered drains were constructed alongside streets to maintain hygiene and prevent flooding, reflecting the civilization's emphasis on sanitation.
 
• Major cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa displayed this layout, with residential and commercial areas systematically organized.
 
• This urban feature highlights the technological and administrative proficiency of the Indus Valley people.

• **Sophisticated Drainage:** A covered, underground drainage system connected house drains (from kitchens/bathrooms) to main street sewers, with manholes for cleaning, highlighting focus on hygiene. 
 
• **Standardized Construction:** Uniform, baked bricks of consistent sizes were used for buildings, roads, and drains, showing advanced standardization. 
 
• **Residential Planning:** Houses often had courtyards, bathrooms, and sometimes two stories, with doors opening onto smaller lanes, not main streets. 
 
• **Public Structures:** Large structures like granaries, assembly halls, and the famous Great Bath (Mohenjo-Daro) served communal purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with both its abbreviation and its function?

options.text: ROM – Read Only Memory – Stores boot instructions needed when the computer is powered on
PCB – Printed Chip Base – Transfers data from CPU to display
CPU – Central Processing Unit – Stores user files permanently
RAM – Read Access Memory – Runs the operating system even after power is off

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM – Read Only Memory – Stores boot instructions needed when the computer is powered on**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ROM (Read Only Memory)** is a non-volatile memory that retains data even when the computer is powered off.
 
• It stores essential instructions and data necessary for the computer to boot up, commonly known as the **firmware or BIOS** (Basic Input/Output System).
 
• The primary function of ROM is to **store boot instructions**, making it critical for initializing hardware and loading the operating system.
 
• Unlike RAM, the contents of ROM cannot be modified or erased during normal operation, ensuring the integrity of the boot process.
 
• ROM is utilized in various embedded systems, gaming consoles, and other devices where permanent instructions are required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PCB – Printed Chip Base**

 
 
• The correct abbreviation for PCB is **Printed Circuit Board**, not Printed Chip Base.
 
• PCB is a physical board used to connect electronic components using conductive pathways, tracks, and pads.
 
• It acts as the foundation for most electronic devices but does not perform the function of transferring data from the CPU to the display.
 
 
 
• **CPU – Central Processing Unit**
 
 
• The CPU is the **brain of the computer** and is responsible for executing instructions from programs.
 
• It does not store user files permanently; this function is typically handled by storage devices like **HDDs or SSDs**.
 
• The CPU processes data, performs calculations, and coordinates the operations of the entire computer system.
 
 
 
• **RAM – Read Access Memory**
 
 
• The correct term for RAM is **Random Access Memory**, not Read Access Memory.
 
• RAM is a volatile memory that temporarily stores data and instructions that the CPU needs while running programs.
 
• It does not retain data after the computer is powered off, unlike what is stated in the option.

questions.question: Which of the following tribunals deals specifically with service-related matters of public servants?

• It deals specifically with service matters of **civil servants**, such as promotions, transfers, pay scales, disciplinary actions, and other employment-related grievances.
 
• CAT has jurisdiction over **Central Government employees**, except members of the armed forces, officers and employees of the Supreme Court, and employees of state government services.
 
• The tribunal functions under the **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985**, and its decisions are binding, though appeals can be made to the High Court or Supreme Court in specific cases.

• Their density represents the strength of the magnetic field.

• His views clashed with Gandhi's, leading to significant debates during the conference.

questions.question: Clear skies, rising temperatures, and moist land — conditions commonly referred to as ‘October heat’ — are associated with which of the following in the Indian context?

__
 
• The phenomenon of "October heat" occurs due to the retreating monsoon, where monsoon winds withdraw from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• This phase is marked by **clear skies, high temperatures, and humid conditions**, especially during October.
 
• The retreating monsoon is characterized by the movement of dry winds from the **northwest**, which replace the moist monsoon winds.
 
• During this period, the land is moist from the monsoon rains, and the high temperatures create conditions for increased humidity, leading to the term "October heat."
 
• The retreating monsoon also contributes to the formation of **cyclones in the Bay of Bengal**, which typically occur during October and November.

• While these depressions do occur, their formation is more prominent during the pre-monsoon (April-May) and post-monsoon (October-November) periods, not directly related to October heat.
 
• The cyclonic activity in the Arabian Sea is typically less frequent compared to the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Wind striking the Western Coast**
 
 
• This option refers to the southwest monsoon winds, which bring rainfall to the western coast of India from June to September.
 
• These winds lose their strength by October as the monsoon season recedes, giving way to retreating monsoon winds. Thus, it is unrelated to October heat.
 
 
 
• **Cyclonic Depressions of Bay of Bengal**
 
 
• While cyclonic depressions in the Bay of Bengal are common during the retreating monsoon season (October-November), they are not directly responsible for October heat.
 
• These depressions often lead to heavy rainfall and cyclones along the eastern coast of India.
 
• However, they are an indirect result of the retreating monsoon rather than a cause of October heat.

questions.question: The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 650. The greater of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find **consecutive natural numbers** whose product is 650, find the **square root** of 650.

√650 ≈ 25.49

The numbers must be around 25 and 26.

Check: 25 × 26 = 650.

The **greater number** is 26.

**∴ The correct answer is 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Product of two **consecutive natural numbers** = 650.

Let the two **consecutive natural numbers** be **x** and **(x + 1)**.

**Formula:** x × (x + 1) = 650

⇒ x² + x − 650 = 0

⇒ x² + 26x − 25x − 650 = 0

⇒ x(x + 26) − 25(x + 26) = 0

⇒ (x + 26)(x − 25) = 0

⇒ x = 25 or x = −26

Since the numbers are **natural numbers**, x = 25.

⇒ Smaller number = 25

⇒ **Greater number** = x + 1 = 25 + 1 = 26.

**∴ The correct answer is 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Numbers

Numbers that follow each other in order from smallest to largest without any gaps (e.g., n, n+1, n+2).

Quadratic Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the product of roots is c/a and the sum is −b/a.

Natural Numbers

Positive integers starting from 1 (1, 2, 3, ...) used for counting and ordering.</p

questions.question: The average weight of Ram, Anwar and Amit is 45 kg. If the average weight of Ram and Anwar is 44 kg and that of Anwar and Amit is 42 kg, then the weight of Anwar (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Weight of **Ram, Anwar, Amit** = 45 × 3 = 135 kg.

Combined Weight of (**Ram + Anwar**) and (**Anwar + Amit**) = (44 × 2) + (42 × 2).

Total of subsets = 88 + 84 = 172 kg.

Weight of **Anwar** (overlapping person) = Sum of subsets − Total sum = 172 − 135 = 37 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 37 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of (**Ram** + **Anwar** + **Amit**) = 45 kg

Average weight of (**Ram** + **Anwar**) = 44 kg

Average weight of (**Anwar** + **Amit**) = 42 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec3fd97ee7564c2da92410f8bf8054d30f9cc4a75fc1776e9c665f778ecf2a50.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Weight of (**Ram** + **Anwar** + **Amit**) = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

⇒ Weight of (**Ram** + **Anwar**) = 44 × 2 = 88 kg

⇒ Weight of (**Anwar** + **Amit**) = 42 × 2 = 84 kg

⇒ Let weights be R, Anwar, and Amit respectively.

⇒ (R + Anwar) + (Anwar + Amit) = 88 + 84

⇒ R + 2 × Anwar + Amit = 172 kg

⇒ Anwar = (R + 2 × Anwar + Amit) − (R + Anwar + Amit)

⇒ Anwar = 172 − 135

⇒ Anwar = 37 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations). Sum = Average × Count.

Overlapping Middle Term

If in a group of 'n' people, the average of first 'm' and last 'k' are given such that (m + k) = n + 1, the middle term = (Sum of m) + (Sum of k) − (Total Sum of n).

Deviation Method

Anwar's Weight = Total Average + Deviation₁ + Deviation₂ = 45 + 2 × (44 − 45) + 2 × (42 − 45) = 45 − 2 − 6 = 37 kg.</p

questions.question: In covering a distance of 102 km, Amit takes 8 hours more than Vinay. If Amit doubles his speed, then he would take 9 hours less than Vinay. Amit's speed is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Let **Amit's speed** be S₁ and S₂. Speed ratio S₁ : S₂ = 1 : 2.

Since distance is constant, **Time ratio** T₁ : T₂ = 2 : 1.

Difference in units = 2 − 1 = 1 unit.

Actual **Time difference** = 8 hours (late) + 9 hours (early) = 17 hours.

∴ 1 unit = 17 hours → Original time (T₁) = 2 units = 34 hours.

**Amit's speed** = Distance ÷ Time = 102 ÷ 34 = 3 km/hr.

questions.question: Find the value of x satisfying: 3(3x² − 6) − 3(3x² + 5x − 7) = 19
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factor out the common multiplier **3**: 3[(3x² − 6) − (3x² + 5x − 7)] = 19

Subtract the expressions inside the bracket: 3[3x² − 6 − 3x² − 5x + 7] = 19

Eliminate the quadratic terms: 3[−5x + 1] = 19

Simplify and solve: −15x + 3 = 19 ⇒ −15x = 16

**∴ The correct answer is −16/15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3(3x² − 6) − 3(3x² + 5x − 7) = 19

Apply the **distributive property** to expand the brackets:

⇒ (9x² − 18) − (9x² + 15x − 21) = 19

Remove the parentheses and change the signs for the second term:

⇒ 9x² − 18 − 9x² − 15x + 21 = 19

Combine **like terms**:

⇒ (9x² − 9x²) − 15x + (−18 + 21) = 19

⇒ −15x + 3 = 19

Isolate the **variable x** by moving the constant to the right side:

⇒ −15x = 19 − 3

⇒ −15x = 16

⇒ x = −16/15

**∴ The correct answer is −16/15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: Gopal, Hema, and Uday invest ₹1,130, ₹1,030, and ₹1,840, respectively, to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹1,800, then what is the share of Uday in the profit?

To find the **LCM** of decimals, make the number of **decimal places** equal.

Numbers: 2.900 and 0.031

questions.question: Kiran can do a certain piece of work in 26 days. Kiran and Garima can together do the same work in 13 days, and Kiran, Garima and Mehak can do the same work together in 10 days. In how many days can Kiran and Mehak do the same work together?

**Efficiency** of (Kiran + Garima + Mehak) = 130 ÷ 10 = 13 units/day.

Efficiency of **Mehak** = (K+G+M) − (K+G) = 13 − 10 = 3 units/day.

Time for (Kiran + Mehak) = 130 ÷ (5 + 3) = 130 ÷ 8 = 65/4 days.

⇒ Efficiency of **Kiran** = 5

⇒ Efficiency of **Garima** = (K + G) − K = 10 − 5 = 5

⇒ Efficiency of **Mehak** = (K + G + M) − (K + G) = 13 − 10 = 3

⇒ Combined efficiency of **Kiran and Mehak** = 5 + 3 = 8 units/day

⇒ Time taken by **Kiran and Mehak** = 130 ÷ 8 = 65/4 days

questions.question: Sapna invested ₹22,400 on simple interest, partly at 12% per annum and partly at 8% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 4 years, then find the sum invested at 12% per annum (in ₹).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When **Simple Interests** are equal for the same time duration, the ratio of sums is the **inverse ratio** of their interest rates.

Ratio of investments P₁ : P₂ = 1/r₁ : 1/r₂ = 1/12 : 1/8 = 2 : 3.

Total ratio units = 2 + 3 = 5 units.

5 units → ₹22,400 ⇒ 1 unit = 22,400 ÷ 5 = ₹4,480.

Sum at 12% (P₁) = 2 units = 2 × 4,480 = ₹8,960.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,960.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total Principal = ₹22,400, Rate₁ = 12%, Rate₂ = 8%, Time = 4 years.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4f5680f6d33516415b2a13f9c53c8020852436226cfab0ebfbbb0d44d897d92.png] 

⇒ Let the sum invested at 12% be P₁ and at 8% be P₂.

⇒ SI₁ = (P₁ × 12 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P₂ × 8 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ Given: SI₁ = SI₂

⇒ (P₁ × 12 × 4) ÷ 100 = (P₂ × 8 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 12P₁ = 8P₂

⇒ P₁ ÷ P₂ = 8 ÷ 12 = 2 ÷ 3

⇒ Sum of ratios = 2 + 3 = 5 units

⇒ 5 units = 22,400

⇒ P₁ = (2 ÷ 5) × 22,400

⇒ P₁ = 2 × 4,480 = 8,960

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,960.**

**__Additional Information__**

Equal Simple Interest Property

If a sum is divided into 'n' parts such that interest on each part is equal, the ratio of principal amounts is P₁:P₂:...:Pₙ = 1/(r₁t₁) : 1/(r₂t₂) : ... : 1/(rₙtₙ).

Equal Amount Property

If a sum is divided into parts such that the total amount (Principal + SI) after respective periods is equal, the ratio is P₁:P₂ = 1/(100+r₁t₁) : 1/(100+r₂t₂).

Simple Interest Formula

Interest is calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount for the entire duration: SI = (P × R × T)/100.
